subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should bundled Codex and Copilot harnesses permanently receive the private lifecycle reset queue, or must core expose a narrower owner-specific bridge that never hands harness code the raw queue?
rationale: The patch rejects spoofed harness IDs, but still creates a new privileged boundary for bundled plugin-owned harness code; repository policy requires explicit ownership intent for that permanent authority.

options.title: Use a narrow host bridge
options.body: Keep the raw queue core-private and expose only a current-session reset callback while core owns validation, queueing, and commit notification.

options.title: Approve bundled raw authority
options.body: Explicitly bless registered bundled Codex and Copilot harness instances as trusted queue recipients with dedicated compatibility and security contracts.

options.title: Limit to OpenClaw harness
options.body: Ship reset support only for the built-in harness until a generic trusted lifecycle capability is designed.

recommendation.title: Use a narrow host bridge
recommendation.body: Keep the raw queue core-private and expose only a current-session reset callback while core owns validation, queueing, and commit notification.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to Codex harness selection, native compaction, and the adjacent persistent-schema compatibility decision.
